original_question: Let R(x) = sum_{n>=0} s(n)x^n be a power series in Z[[x]] that is algebraic over Q(x) and unramified at x = 0. Suppose that for all sufficiently large primes p one has s(p) == 0 mod p. Characterize all such algebraic functions with this Fermat property, both in general and inside a fixed algebraic function field Q(x, U) where U is unramified at x = 0.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1 of arXiv:1609.09842, with the immediately following Problem 2 as the paper's sharpened fixed-field refinement. The note does not present a Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 sequence; for this draft, the relevant official target is Problem 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core content very well: it asks about algebraic functions over Q(x), unramified at x = 0, satisfying the prime-index congruence condition a_p ≡ 0 mod p for all sufficiently large primes, and it keeps the paper's two-part scope of classifying them both globally and inside a fixed algebraic function field Q(x,U) with U unramified at x = 0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
missing_details: The paper does not state the problem for an integral power series R(x) in Z[[x]]; it states it for an algebraic function over Q(x), later explicitly identifying such a function with its Laurent expansion at x = 0. So your draft is slightly narrower than the official formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The condition is given on the p-th coefficient of the chosen local expansion at x = 0, with the branch required to be unramified there; this Laurent-series viewpoint is implicit in your draft but explicit in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The paper introduces a name for the condition: such an object is called an 'algebraic function with a Fermat property.' Your draft uses the idea but not the paper's term. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The phrase 'for all sufficiently large primes p' should be read as 'for all but finitely many prime numbers p.' The paper immediately notes a normalization: one may multiply the function by an integer so that the congruence becomes valid for all primes. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

For the fixed-field part, the paper's next refinement is stronger than a bare characterization inside Q(x,U): Problem 2 asks for the structure of the relevant abelian groups attached to a fixed algebraic function field Q(x,U). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

Because the paper allows Laurent expansions, it does not build in the restriction n >= 0 or the absence of a pole at x = 0 at the level of Problem 1. Your draft silently imposes that extra regularity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
refined_question: Let F(x) be an algebraic function over Q(x), and identify F with its Laurent expansion at x = 0, F(x) = sum_{n >> -infinity} a_n x^n, choosing a branch that is unramified at x = 0. Assume that for all sufficiently large prime numbers p one has a_p ≡ 0 (mod p). Such an F is called an algebraic function with a Fermat property. Characterize all algebraic functions with a Fermat property, both in general and within any prescribed algebraic function field Q(x,U), where U is algebraic over Q(x) and unramified at x = 0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the paper's Section 1 open problem on 'algebraic functions with a Fermat property': the official statement is almost exactly your global-plus-fixed-field characterization question. The main adjustments needed to make it paper-faithful are (i) removing the unnecessary restriction to Z[[x]], because the paper speaks of algebraic functions over Q(x); (ii) making explicit that the object is viewed via its Laurent expansion at x = 0 on an unramified branch; and (iii) noting that the paper's immediate refinement of the fixed-field part is Problem 2, which reframes that part as a group-structure question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
